title: Aphorism § 79
text:
§ 79



Hitherto syphilis alone has been to some extent known as such a chronic
          miasmatic disease, which when uncured ceases only with the termination of life. Sycosis
          (the condylomatous disease), equally ineradicable by the vital force without proper
          medicinal treatment, was not recognized as a chronic miasmatic disease of a peculiar
          character, which it nevertheless undoubtedly is, and physicians imagined they had cured it
          when they had destroyed the growths upon the skin, but the persisting dyscrasia occasioned
          by it escaped their observation.
